description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of five different model configurations—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, a fourth unlabeled model (represented by a gray bar), and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (light pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue), as reported in the paper “2-Tier SimCSE: Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings.” The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranges from 0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, representing the performance scores for each metric. For each model, three bars are grouped together, with color-coded legend entries indicating which metric each bar represents. The Single-task_baseline model shows Sentiment Accuracy around 0.53, STS Correlation near 0.50, and Paraphrase Accuracy approximately 0.79. The Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout model achieves Sentiment Accuracy of ~0.52, STS Correlation of ~0.58, and Paraphrase Accuracy of ~0.78. The Unsupervised_SimCSE model improves STS Correlation to ~0.71 while maintaining Sentiment Accuracy at ~0.52 and Paraphrase Accuracy at ~0.77. The fourth model (gray bar, unlabeled in legend) shows high STS Correlation (~0.80) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), with Sentiment Accuracy around 0.49. Finally, the 2-Tier SimCSE model achieves the highest STS Correlation (~0.81), Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), and Sentiment Accuracy (~0.49). The chart visually emphasizes the consistent improvement in STS Correlation across models, particularly with 2-Tier SimCSE, while Paraphrase Accuracy remains relatively stable across all models, and Sentiment Accuracy shows more variation.
